title: The sign given to the house of David
source_text: Ἵνα δὲ μὴ δοκῶμεν ἀπὸ λέξεως Ἑβραϊκῆς τοῖς μὴ καταλαμβάνουσι, πότερον συγκαταθετέον αὐτῇ ἢ μὴ, φέρειν παραμυθίαν περὶ τοῦ προφήτην εἰρηκέναι ἐκ παρθένου τεχθήσεσθαι τοῦτον, ἐφ᾿ οὗ τῇ γενέσει λέλεκται τὸ „μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεὸς“, φέρε ἐπ᾿ αὐτῆς τῆς λέξεως παραμυθησώμεθα τὸ λεγόμενον. ὁ μὲν κύριος ἀναγέγραπται εἰρηκέναι τῷ Ἄχαζ· „αἴτησαι σεαυτῷ σημεῖον παρὰ κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ σου εἰς βάθος ἢ εἰς ὕψος,“ ἑξῆς δὲ τὸ διδόμενον σημεῖον τὸ „ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν.“ ποῖον οὖν σημεῖον τὸ νεάνιδα, μὴ παρθένον τεκεῖν; καὶ τίνι μᾶλλον ἁρμόζει γεννῆσαι „Ἐμμανουὴλ,“ τουτέστι „μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεὸς,“ ἆρα γυναικὶ συνουσιασθείσῃ καὶ διὰ πάθους γυναικείου συλλαβούσῃ ἢ ἔτι καθαρᾷ καὶ ἁγνῇ καὶ παρθένῳ; ταύτῃ γὰρ πρέπει γεννᾶν γέννημα, ἐφ᾿ ᾧ τεχθέντι λέγεται τὸ „μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεός.“ ἐὰν δὲ καὶ οὕτως εὑρεσιλογῇ λέγων ὅτι τῷ Ἄχαζ εἴρηται· „αἴτησαι σεαυτῷ σημεῖον παρὰ κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ σου,“ ἀπαντήσομεν· κατὰ τοὺς χρόνους τοῦ Ἄχαζ τίς ἐγεννήθη, ἐφ᾿ οἷ τῇ γενέσει λέγεται τὸ „Ἐμμανουὴλ, ὅ ἐστι μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὁ θεός,·“ εἰ γὰρ οὐδεὶς εὑρεθήσεται, δηλονότι τὸ τῷ Ἄχαζ εἰρημένον τῷ οἴκῳ εἴρηται Δαυὶδ διὰ τὸ „ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυὶδ“ ἀναγεγράφθαι τὸν σωτῆρα γεγονέναι „τὸ κατὰ σάρκα“· ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ „σημεῖον“ τοῦτο „εἰς βάθος ἢ εἰς ὕψος“ λέγεται εἶναι, ἐπεὶ „ὁ καταβὰς οὗτός ἐστι καὶ ὁ ἀναβὰς ὑπεράνω πάντων τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἵνα πληρώσῃ τὰ πάντα.“ ταῦτα δὲ λέγω ὡς πρὸς τὸν Ἰουδαῖον συγκατατιθέμενον τῇ προφητείᾳ. λεγέτω δὲ καὶ Κέλσος ἤ τις τῶν σὺν αὐτῷ, ποίῳ νῷ ὁ προφήτης περὶ μελλόντων ἢ ταῦτα ἢ ἕτερα λέγει, ὁπόσα ἀναγέγραπται ἐν ταῖς προφητείαις· ἆρα γὰρ προγνωστικῷ μελλόντων ἢ οὔ; εἰ μὲν γὰρ προγνωστικῷ μελλόντων, θεῖον εἶχον πνεῦμα οἱ προφῆται· εἰ δ᾿ οὐ προγνωστικῷ μελλόντων, παραστησάτω τὸν νοῦν τοῦ ἀποτολμῶντος καὶ λέγοντος περὶ μελλόντων καὶ θαυμαζομένου παρὰ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἐπὶ προφητείᾳ.
pass_a_gloss: So that we may not seem, from a Hebrew word (λέξεως Ἑβραϊκῆς), to bring to those who do not grasp (καταλαμβάνουσι) whether one should assent (συγκαταθετέον) to it or not, an assurance/proof (παραμυθίαν) about the prophet having said that this one will be born of a virgin, at whose birth 'with us God' has been said, come, let us make good (παραμυθησώμεθα) what is said from the wording itself (ἐπ᾿ αὐτῆς τῆς λέξεως). The Lord is recorded to have said to Ahaz: 'ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God into depth or into height', and next the sign given (διδόμενον σημεῖον): 'behold the virgin will have in womb (ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει) and bear a son'. What sort of sign then [is] a young woman (νεάνιδα), not a virgin, giving birth? And to whom is it more fitting (ἁρμόζει) to bear 'Emmanuel', that is 'with us God': to a woman who has had intercourse (συνουσιασθείσῃ) and conceived through womanly passion (πάθους γυναικείου), or to one still pure (καθαρᾷ) and chaste (ἁγνῇ) and virgin? For to this one it is fitting (πρέπει) to bear an offspring (γέννημα) at whose birth is said 'with us God'. And if even so he quibbles (εὑρεσιλογῇ), saying that it was said to Ahaz 'ask for yourself a sign...', we shall reply: in the times of Ahaz who was born, at whose birth is said 'Emmanuel, which is with us God'? For if none will be found, clearly what was said to Ahaz was said to the house of David, because the Saviour (σωτῆρα) is recorded to have come 'from the seed of David according to the flesh'; but also this 'sign' is said to be 'into depth or into height', since 'the one who descended (καταβάς) is the same also who ascended (ἀναβάς) above all the heavens, that he might fill all things'. These things I say as to the Jew assenting to the prophecy. But let Celsus also say, or one of those with him, with what kind of mind (ποίῳ νῷ) the prophet says about future things these or others, as many as are recorded in the prophecies: with [a mind] foreknowing (προγνωστικῷ) the future or not? For if foreknowing the future, the prophets had a divine spirit (θεῖον πνεῦμα); but if not foreknowing, let him present (παραστησάτω) the mind of one who ventures (ἀποτολμῶντος) and speaks about the future and is admired among the Jews for prophecy.
pass_b_english: But so that we may not seem to rest on a Hebrew word, offering people who cannot tell whether to accept it or not our proof that the prophet said this child would be born of a virgin, the child of whose birth the words “God with us” have been spoken, let us make the point good from the wording itself. The Lord is recorded as having said to Ahaz: “Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, in the depth or in the height” (Isaiah 7:11), and next comes the sign that is given: “Behold, the virgin shall be with child and bear a son” (Isaiah 7:14). What sort of sign, then, would it be for a young woman who was not a virgin to give birth? And to whom is it more fitting to bear “Emmanuel,” that is, “God with us” (Matthew 1:23)? To a woman who has had intercourse and conceived through a woman’s passion, or to one still pure and chaste and a virgin? For it is fitting for her to bring forth the offspring at whose birth it is said, “God with us.”

And if he quibbles in this way too, saying that the words “Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God” were spoken to Ahaz, we shall answer: who was born in the time of Ahaz at whose birth it is said, “Emmanuel, which is, God with us”? For if no one is to be found, then clearly what was said to Ahaz was said to the house of David (Isaiah 7:13), because the Saviour is recorded to have come “from the seed of David according to the flesh” (Romans 1:3). Moreover, this sign is said to be “in the depth or in the height,” since “he who descended is the very one who also ascended far above all the heavens, that he might fill all things” (Ephesians 4:10). I say this as to a Jew who accepts the prophecy.

But let Celsus too, or any of his party, say with what kind of mind the prophet speaks of the future, in these words or in any of the others recorded in the prophecies. Is it a mind that foreknows the future, or not? If it foreknows the future, the prophets had a divine Spirit. If it does not foreknow the future, let him explain the mind of a man who ventures to speak about the future and is admired among the Jews for prophecy.

choices.choice: Isaiah 7:14 is here quoted in the form ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει ('shall be with child'), the wording of Matthew 1:23, where 1.34 had λήψεται ('shall conceive'); the difference is kept. 'Emmanuel, which is, God with us' follows the gloss of Matthew 1:23. The reference to 'the house of David' points back to Isaiah 7:13 quoted in 1.34. Romans 1:3 is quoted (ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυὶδ κατὰ σάρκα); Ephesians 4:10 is quoted closely, with 'depth or height' read against descent and ascent. The opening sentence is involved in the Greek (the purpose clause governs φέρειν παραμυθίαν); it is kept as one sentence in natural order. θεῖον πνεῦμα has no article and is phrased generically for a pagan reader; 'Spirit' is capitalised because Origen means the Spirit of God who spoke in the prophets.
